top_story_title: FBI warns FortiBleed attacks are ongoing: attackers are locking admins out of FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways
top_story_summary: The FBI has issued a warning that the attack campaign reported as "FortiBleed" is still active against internet-exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways. Unlike most edge-device campaigns, the reported goal is not quiet persistence: the attackers create new administrative accounts and then delete existing accounts and passwords, locking the legitimate administrators out of their own perimeter device. Two independent reports in this cycle (BleepingComputer citing the FBI, and SecurityWeek) describe the same behaviour.
top_actions: Confirm right now that you can authenticate to every internet-facing FortiGate and that an out-of-band path (console server, serial, dedicated management link) works - verify this before you start changing anything.
Export and store a current configuration backup off-device for every FortiGate and SSL VPN gateway, and verify the export is readable.
Remove the administrative interface (HTTPS/SSH/API) from all internet-facing interfaces; restrict administration to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
Audit the local administrator list, API users and admin profiles for accounts you did not create, and compare against your last known-good configuration backup.

Check the running version against Fortinet's advisory and schedule the upgrade to the vendor's fixed build - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as no fixed version is stated in these reports.
executive_summary: The FBI says FortiBleed attacks against exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways are ongoing, with attackers creating admin accounts and deleting existing ones to lock legitimate administrators out. This is the one to act on today.

Cisco published a large 7 October 2026 bundle dominated by NX-OS: unauthenticated remote code execution as root on Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches via MPLS OAM (CVE-2026-76465, CVSS 9.8), further RCE via NGOAM, RCE via NX-API, and a critical NX-OS hardening release (CVE-2026-76453/76455/76456/76457/76458/76459, CVSS 9.8). None have workarounds - the fix is the upgrade.

Cisco APIC, the ACI fabric controller, takes three issues including API command injection to root and file access that exposes key material usable to elevate to root on managed switches. A fabric controller compromise is a whole-fabric compromise.
SonicWall shipped hotfixes for four SMA1000 flaws, the worst a pre-authentication SSRF rated CVSS 10.0; SonicWall states it has no evidence any of the four is being exploited.

TP-Link is facing US state lawsuits over ISP router flaws, with SEC Consult now publishing technical detail on the vulnerabilities named in the complaint - relevant to anyone with ISP-supplied TP-Link CPE in branch or home-office estates.

Cisco's advance notification ties this disclosure format - findings grouped by CWE with one CVE per grouping - to its stated response to AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery, so triage must now key on model and version, not CVE count.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Inventory Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches and check whether MPLS OAM is configured; the advisory's Vulnerable Products section defines the exact feature condition.

**Cisco** — Upgrade NX-OS to the fixed release from the advisory - validate the ISSU/hitless path for spine and distribution switches first, and verify image integrity against Cisco's published hash before loading.
**Cisco** — Check whether NGOAM is enabled on each Nexus 3000/9000; the per-vulnerability feature conditions are in the advisory's Vulnerable Products section and are not uniform.
**Cisco** — Upgrade NX-OS to the fixed release, bundling this with the MPLS OAM and NX-API upgrades into a single change window rather than three.
**Cisco** — Determine where NX-API (the 'feature nxapi' HTTP/HTTPS server) is enabled, and disable it on every switch that no automation actually drives.
**Cisco** — Upgrade NX-OS to the fixed release from the advisory.
**Cisco** — Treat this as the anchor of a single NX-OS change window covering the MPLS OAM, NGOAM, NX-API, control-plane DoS and Python sandbox advisories together.
**Cisco** — Match your switches to the advisory by platform and running version rather than by CVE ID, since each CVE covers a class of defects.

ai_defenses.solution: Strengthening the Foundation: A Predictable, Customer-Focused Response to AI-Accelerated Vulnerability Discovery
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Cisco's documented change to how PSIRT discloses vulnerabilities, referenced from the advance notification for the 7 October 2026 advisories. In this bundle it takes the form of proactive internal security reviews published as 'security hardening releases', with internally discovered findings grouped by Common Weakness Enumeration class and a single CVE ID assigned per CWE grouping to streamline customer patching.

headlines.title: Cisco Nexus 3000 and 9000 Series Switches MPLS OAM Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
headlines.summary: An unauthenticated attacker can get root on Cisco Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches by sending one crafted MPLS echo-request; CVE-2026-76465, CVSS 9.8, no workaround.

headlines.title: Cisco Nexus 3000 and 9000 Series Switches NGOAM Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
headlines.summary: Multiple NGOAM flaws in Cisco NX-OS let an unauthenticated attacker run code as root on Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches with crafted packets; no workaround exists.

headlines.title: Cisco NX-OS Software NX-API Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
headlines.summary: A crafted HTTP request to the NX-API on Cisco NX-OS gives an unauthenticated attacker arbitrary code execution as root, or crashes the device into a reload.

headlines.title: Cisco NX-OS Software Security Hardening Release: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco's NX-OS hardening release fixes internally found vulnerabilities rated Critical at CVSS 9.8 (CVE-2026-76453/76455/76456/76457/76458/76459), with no workarounds available.

headlines.title: FBI: Ongoing FortiBleed attacks lock out FortiGate VPN admins
headlines.summary: The FBI warns FortiBleed attacks are still running against exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, and are locking legitimate administrators out of the devices.

headlines.title: SonicWall Patches CVSS 10.0 Pre-Authentication SSRF Flaw in SMA1000 Appliances
headlines.summary: SonicWall hotfixed four SMA1000 flaws, the worst a pre-authentication SSRF rated CVSS 10.0 that lets an attacker without a login reach internal functions through the remote-access gateway.
